newsitem.title: USA: OfficeMax seen likely acquirer, not target.
newsitem.headline: OfficeMax seen likely acquirer, not target.

text.p: OfficeMax Inc is more likely to be an acquirer than a target in what analysts see as a continuing consolidation among office supply retailers.
"I think they'll be an acquirer," analyst Dana Telsey of Bear, Stearns & Co said. "They have a strong balance sheet and a large cash position."

Christopher Vroom of Alex. Brown & Sons agreed. "The company has indicated it will make an acquisition in a complementary business... and that any potential acquisition would be accretive to earnings and therefore positive," he said. "We concur with that viewpoint."

OfficeMax officials declined comment Friday on a story in the November 25 issue of Business Week magazine that said OfficeMax was likely to become involved as the industry consolidates further, either as a "hunter -- or prey."
The 530-store chain previously said it was pursuing possible acquisitions.
In September, competitors Office Depot Inc and Staples Inc proposed merging in a stock swap. After the announcement, OfficeMax said it was reviewing its options.
On Friday afternoon, OfficeMax stock was up 3/8 to 14-3/8 in trading on the New York Stock Exchange.

Vroom said he thought it was unlikely that OfficeMax management would want the company -- once part of Kmart Corp -- to be acquired. But, he said, OfficeMax could gain another growth leg by making an acquisition of its own.

After the Staples-Office Depot announcement, the company said it would step up its store expansion program this year and next. It also has expanded its store-within-a-store copy centers and furniture centers, while opening outlets outside the United States.
